name: Question 12
problem:
Which of the following vector-valued functions are differentiable at $t=0?$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨|t-1|,\,7t+6,\,3⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨1,\,{t}^{2},\,t⟩ \\ h(t) & =⟨{t}^{3}+1,\,\sqrt[3]{t},\,2t+3⟩\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
All of these vector-valued functions are defined at $t=0.$ 

A vector-valued function is differentiable at a point if and only if each of its components is differentiable at that point. 

Let's consider the functions one-by-one. 

- We differentiate $f(t)$ to find ${f}^{′}(0).$
Note, that the derivative of $|t-1|$ at  $t=0$ coincides with the derivative of $(1-t),$ so, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(0) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(7t+6),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,7,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since each component of ${f}^{′}(t)$ is  defined  at $t=0$, we conclude that $f(t)$ is differentiable at this point.

- Next, we differentiate $g(t)$  to find ${g}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2t,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since each component of ${g}^{′}(t)$ is defined   at $t=0$, we conclude that $g(t)$ is differentiable at this point.

- Finally, we differentiate $h(t)$ to find ${h}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt[3]{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+3)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2},\,\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{t}^{2}}},\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Since the second component of this vector, $\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{t}^{2}}}$, is undefined at $t=0$,  we conclude that the function $h(t)$ is not differentiable at $t=0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$f(t)$ and $g(t)$ only."

html:
Question 12
?

Which of the following vector-valued functions are differentiable at t=0?

f(t)=⟨|t−1|,7t+6,3⟩g(t)=⟨1,t2,t⟩h(t)=⟨t3+1,t3,2t+3⟩

a
All of them are differentiable at t=0
b
f(t) and g(t) only
c
f(t) and h(t) only
d
g(t) only
e
None of them are differentiable at t=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

All of these vector-valued functions are defined at t=0.

A vector-valued function is differentiable at a point if and only if each of its components is differentiable at that point.

Let's consider the functions one-by-one.

  • We differentiate f(t) to find f′(0). Note, that the derivative of |t−1| at t=0 coincides with the derivative of (1−t), so, we have f′(0)=⟨ddt(1−t),ddt(7t+6),ddt(3)⟩=⟨−1,7,0⟩ Since each component of f′(t) is defined at t=0, we conclude that f(t) is differentiable at this point.

  • Next, we differentiate g(t) to find g′(t): g′(t)=⟨ddt(1),ddt(t2),ddt(t)⟩=⟨0,2t,1⟩ Since each component of g′(t) is defined at t=0, we conclude that g(t) is differentiable at this point.

  • Finally, we differentiate h(t) to find h′(t): h′(t)=⟨ddt(t3+1),ddt(t3),ddt(2t+3)⟩=⟨3t2,13t23,2⟩ Since the second component of this vector, 13t23, is undefined at t=0, we conclude that the function h(t) is not differentiable at t=0.

Therefore, the correct answer is "f(t) and g(t) only."
